summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis following fundoplication was admitted for acute abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting that began after an upper GI series with barium. The symptoms were consistent with a gastroparesis flare, likely triggered by the barium load. Imaging showed no bowel obstruction, with barium present throughout the colon. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, and anti-nausea medications including IV Reglan and lorazepam. Her symptoms improved, she tolerated a full liquid diet, and was discharged home on hospital day three in stable condition. Follow-up was recommended for mildly elevated alkaline phosphatase and ongoing gastroparesis management.
